SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: extract_text(layout=True) broken: reconstructing readable text from positioned glyphs is the same problem OCR layout solves.
cluster_list tolerance grouping is wrong; grouping glyph positions into lines/words is the core of reading text off a page.
Word extraction returns wrong direction for rotated text; spatial text recovery from a rendered document.
Character width calculation wrong; glyph metrics drive where characters land, which is what makes extracted text legible.
Text extraction fails on certain PDFs; getting readable text out of a rendered document, the non-OCR half of this task.
PageImage crop renders the wrong region; reasoning about page-to-image coordinates, the space OCR preprocessing works in.
Parser error recovery on incomplete code; making sense of imperfect source text is exactly the post-OCR problem.
Tokenizer mishandles unicode identifiers and strings; robust tokenization of arbitrary source characters.
Recovering the right text from ambiguous bytes; the noisy-recognition analogue of OCR, judged on exact decoded text.
ASCII QR rendering broken; encoding data into a visual grid, the inverse direction of reading code out of a picture.

Grammar cache loading failure in a parser generator; parsing-infrastructure domain, little of this task's extraction or execution skill.

notes: OCR/image-as-specification exists in exactly one corpus: TMax (~800 instructions mention tesseract/OCR; ~55 of them put the algorithm itself in the image). RTS, TerminalWorld, SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench contain zero OCR tasks, so the honest final_top10 is all TMax and I did not dilute it. For the other four corpora I scored against the task's second half instead (faithfully executing or re-implementing a snippet to one exact value) and, for SWE-Smith, against the closest domain available (pdfplumber/pdfminer text-from-rendered-page extraction). The SWE-Rebench pfp cluster (an interpreter for 010 Editor binary templates) is the best non-TMax skill match and was almost entirely missed by the retrievers. RTS and TerminalWorld ranks 6-10 are filler; the shortlists there were dominated by 'write string to /app/output.txt' boilerplate, which I deliberately ranked low even though it matched lexically.
